thread:
michelle: Heads up — after yesterday's kernel-routing tweak we saw a sharp KV cache hit-rate regression on prod batch workers (canary region). Hit-rate went from ~88% to ~62% for the exact same traffic shape. Link to flame/profiler: https://internal/redwood/prof/17777 :eyes:
raj: ugh. timeline? which tweak exactly (kernel selection or routing policy)?
eva: saw the alert. p50 token-latency slightly up, p95 much more noisy. numbers in the profiler show additional CPU scheduling spikes when requests miss the KV.
michelle: It looks correlated with a change that started routing some requests to the new "small-seq" kernel variant when seq_len <= 8. That kernel doesn't use the same KV probe path (we stubbed it to be conservative), so misses aren't checking the shared prefix cache.
sasha: @michelle can you paste the relevant routing predicate?
michelle: Sure: 
```
if (seq_len <= 8 && batch_size >= 4) route = kernel.small_seq;
else route = kernel.default;
```
We added this to get better throughput on short sequences but didn't wire the KV prefix lookup into small_seq yet.
raj: that would explain it. Short messages were previously hitting prefix cache heavily. Now they hit a kernel that bypasses the cache -> misses blow up and we pay token cost + longer tail.
eva: Quick local repro: emulate mix with 70% short prompts, 30% medium. With old routing hit-rate 86%, with new routing 61%. Misses up from 12% -> 39% on short cohort.
sasha: Two things to consider: 1) teach small_seq to do the same KV probe; 2) change routing to prefer cache-aware variant when prefix tag present. Which is lower-risk?
michelle: Short-term: revert routing predicate in canary to force kernel.default (fast rollback). Mid-term: implement a KV probe shim in small_seq so it uses shared probe code.
raj: Also let's double-check cache keying: we saw some misses because of tool/func-call metadata ordering. The small_seq path was serializing tool args differently (map order vs stable sort). That will create distinct prefix keys even for semantically identical prompts.
eva: Good call. Example bad key differences: 
```
{"tool":"weather","args":{"city":"SF","units":"metric"}}
vs
{"tool":"weather","args":{"units":"metric","city":"SF"}}
```
We should canonicalize tool.args by sorting keys and normalizing whitespace for strings.
sasha: And pin tokenizer version in the cache key. I found a run where a tokenizer patch changed tokenization for emojis, shifting token counts and breaking warmup matching. If kernel selection changes tokenization assumptions that could amplify misses.
michelle: Agree — cache key should include tokenizer_sha or tokenizer_version. Also include a short system_prompt fingerprint (sha256 truncated) so small system prompt edits don't silently poison hit-rate.
raj: For the immediate canary rollback I can push a roll-forward that flips routing back. @sasha can you open a tiny PR to add KV probe to small_seq? We should also add unit tests that assert stable key generation for map-ordering and whitespace noise.
sasha: On it. Will add tests and a runtime flag to enable canonicalization. Also adding an e2e canary test that simulates the short-heavy workload and asserts hit-rate >= 80%.
eva: Perf note: once KV hits recover we'll re-evaluate batching heuristics. The small_seq kernel had better throughput for pure compute but once misses spike, overall latency/throughput degrades. We should add a metric: routing_decision_impact = delta_miss_rate * avg_miss_cost, to bias routing away from non-cache-aware variants for cache-sensitive cohorts.
michelle: Nice idea, metric would help automated routing. Also let's capture a postmortem blurb in incidents channel after rollback.
deploy-bot: canary-deploy (canary-42) rolled back by raj at 1777773380 — reason: KV cache hit-rate regression.
raj: rolled back. Follow-ups: sasha PR for canonicalization + small_seq probe, michelle to open a doc describing routing vs cache-awareness, eva to run a 24h load sim and share numbers.
michelle: I'll draft the doc and include recommended key fields: model_name, model_revision, tokenizer_sha, system_prompt_fingerprint, tool_call_canonicalized, and a normalized prompt string.
sasha: draft PR: https://git.redwood/sasha/kv-smallseq-probe — includes tests and a feature flag `kv_probe_small_seq`.
eva: I'll run the load sim on staging and post graphs later today. If all green, we can re-enable new routing next week behind the feature flag.
raj: thanks everyone. action items tracked in the routing-cache epic. :thumbsup:
